preamble.whatYouWillLearn: You will read and plot points in all four quadrants of a coordinate grid, including points with negative numbers, decimals and fractions. You will use coordinates to find missing corners, lengths and midpoints of shapes. You will also translate (slide) points and shapes and describe translations.
preamble.whyItMatters: Coordinates are a precise way to say exactly where something is. They are the start of graphs, maps and computer drawing, and you will use them all through secondary school maths.
realWorld: Finding a stall on a hawker centre map that uses a grid of letters and numbers
Grab and map apps use coordinates (latitude and longitude) to find your pick-up point
Seat numbers in a cinema or stadium work like rows and columns on a grid
Computer games and drawing apps move characters by changing their x and y coordinates
Ships and planes report their positions to each other using coordinates

subtopics.title: Reading and plotting coordinates
subtopics.summary: Read and plot points in all four quadrants, with whole numbers, decimals and fractions. Always x (across) first, then y (up or down). The four quadrants are numbered anticlockwise from the top right.

subtopics.title: Shapes and lines on the grid
subtopics.summary: Find missing corners of squares, rectangles and parallelograms, and the lengths and midpoints of horizontal and vertical lines.

subtopics.title: Translation
subtopics.summary: Slide points and shapes left, right, up and down, find image coordinates, describe a translation and work backwards to the original.

questions.prompt: Point A is plotted on the grid. Which quadrant is point A in? (Quadrants are numbered anticlockwise, starting from the top right: first = top right, second = top left, third = bottom left, fourth = bottom right.)
questions.solution: Point A is to the LEFT of the y-axis (its x-coordinate is -3) and ABOVE the x-axis (its y-coordinate is 5). Left and up is the top-left part of the grid, which is the second quadrant. (The quadrants are numbered anticlockwise, starting from the top right.)

misconceptions.0: The first quadrant is the top right, where both coordinates are positive. Point A is to the left of the y-axis, so its x-coordinate (-3) is negative.
misconceptions.2: The third quadrant is the bottom left. Point A is above the x-axis, not below it, so its y-coordinate (5) is positive.
misconceptions.3: The fourth quadrant is the bottom right, but point A is on the left and near the top. Count the quadrants anticlockwise from the top right: first, then second (top left), and so on.

questions.prompt: Start at the origin O on the grid. Move 4 units to the right, then 2 units down. What are the coordinates of the point you reach?
questions.solution: Count the squares on the grid from O. Right 4 gives x = 4. Down 2 takes you below the x-axis, so y = -2. Write x first: (4, -2).

misconceptions.1: The coordinates were written the wrong way round. The x-coordinate (left/right) always comes first, then the y-coordinate (up/down).
misconceptions.2: Moving DOWN from the origin gives a negative y-coordinate. 2 units down is y = -2, not 2.
misconceptions.3: The signs are swapped. Right is positive x and down is negative y, so it is (4, -2).

questions.prompt: True or false: The point (0, -6) lies on the y-axis.
questions.solution: The x-coordinate is 0, so the point has not moved left or right from the origin. Every point with x = 0 is on the y-axis (the vertical axis). So the statement is true.

misconceptions.common: Seeing the -6 and thinking the point must be on the x-axis. A point is on the y-axis when its x-coordinate is 0.

questions.prompt: What are the coordinates of the origin, where the x-axis and the y-axis cross? Write them like (x, y).
questions.solution: The origin is the starting point of the grid. You have moved 0 units across and 0 units up, so it is (0, 0).

misconceptions.common: Writing (1, 1) because counting starts at 1. The origin is where both axes are at zero, so it is (0, 0).

questions.prompt: You want to plot the point (-5, 3), starting from the origin. Which move do you make first?
questions.solution: In (-5, 3), x = -5 comes first. x tells you how far to move across: -5 means 5 units to the left. Then y = 3 tells you to move 3 units up.

misconceptions.0: -5 is a negative x-coordinate, which means moving LEFT from the origin, not right.
misconceptions.1: The first number in a coordinate pair is the x-coordinate, so you move across first. A good way to remember: along the corridor, then up the stairs.
misconceptions.3: This uses the second number for the left/right move. The 3 is the y-coordinate and tells you how far up to go.

questions.prompt: Which of these points is in the fourth quadrant? (Quadrants are numbered anticlockwise, starting from the top right: first = top right, second = top left, third = bottom left, fourth = bottom right.)
questions.solution: The fourth quadrant is the bottom-right part of the grid: x positive (right) and y negative (down). (2, -7) is 2 right and 7 down, so it is in the fourth quadrant.

misconceptions.0: This is in the second quadrant (top left). The quadrants are numbered ANTICLOCKWISE from the top right: first (top right), second (top left), third (bottom left), fourth (bottom right).
misconceptions.2: Both coordinates are negative, so this point is in the bottom-left part of the grid, which is the third quadrant.
misconceptions.3: x = 0, so this point is ON the y-axis. Points on an axis do not belong to any quadrant.

questions.prompt: Point P (-4.5, 3) is plotted on the grid. How many units is P from the y-axis?

diagram.alt: A coordinate grid with four quadrants, x from -6 to 6 and y from -5 to 5. Point P is plotted at (-4.5, 3).

questions.solution: The y-axis is the up-and-down line through 0. P is at (-4.5, 3). Its x-coordinate, -4.5, tells you it is 4 1/2 squares to the LEFT of the y-axis (count them on the grid). Distance is always positive, so P is 4.5 units from the y-axis.

misconceptions.common: Answering 3 by using the y-coordinate. The y-coordinate tells you the distance from the x-axis, not from the y-axis. Another slip is writing -4.5: a distance cannot be negative.

questions.prompt: A point is 1/2 a unit to the left of the y-axis and 2 1/2 units above the x-axis. What are its coordinates?
questions.solution: Left of the y-axis by 1/2 means x = -1/2. Above the x-axis by 2 1/2 means y = 2 1/2. So the point is (-1/2, 2 1/2). Fractions work on a grid just like whole numbers.

misconceptions.1: The coordinates are written the wrong way round. The left/right distance (x) comes first, then the up/down distance (y).
misconceptions.2: To the LEFT of the y-axis means the x-coordinate is negative, so x = -1/2.
misconceptions.3: The two numbers have been swapped. Left 1/2 gives x = -1/2 and up 2 1/2 gives y = 2 1/2.

questions.prompt: Put these points in order from LEFT to RIGHT as they would appear on a coordinate grid (furthest left first).
questions.solution: Left to right depends only on the x-coordinate (the first number). The x-coordinates are -3, 1.5, -0.5, -3.5 and 2. From smallest to largest: -3.5, -3, -0.5, 1.5, 2. So the order is (-3.5, 1), (-3, 4), (-0.5, 0), (1.5, -2), (2, 2).

misconceptions.common: Ordering by the y-coordinate, or thinking -3 is further left than -3.5. On the number line -3.5 is to the left of -3.

questions.prompt: Select ALL the points that lie in the third quadrant. (Quadrants are numbered anticlockwise, starting from the top right: first = top right, second = top left, third = bottom left, fourth = bottom right.)
questions.solution: The third quadrant is bottom left, where BOTH coordinates are negative. (-1, -4), (-2.5, -0.5) and (-1/2, -8) have two negative coordinates. Decimals and fractions count just the same as whole numbers.

misconceptions.2: x = 3 is positive, so this point is to the right of the y-axis. It is in the fourth quadrant.
misconceptions.3: y = 2 is positive, so this point is above the x-axis. It is in the second quadrant.
misconceptions.4: x = 0, so this point is on the y-axis itself. Points on an axis are not in any quadrant.

questions.prompt: True or false: (3, -5) and (-5, 3) are the same point.
questions.solution: (3, -5) is 3 right and 5 down (fourth quadrant). (-5, 3) is 5 left and 3 up (second quadrant). The order of the numbers matters, so they are different points. The statement is false.

misconceptions.common: Thinking the order of the numbers does not matter. In a coordinate pair the first number is always x (across) and the second is always y (up or down).

questions.prompt: Point Q is on the x-axis, 3.5 units to the left of the origin. What are the coordinates of Q?
questions.solution: On the x-axis means y = 0. 3.5 units to the left means x = -3.5. So Q is (-3.5, 0).

misconceptions.0: This point is on the y-axis, 3.5 units below the origin. A point on the x-axis has y-coordinate 0, and the -3.5 goes first as the x-coordinate.
misconceptions.1: Being on the x-axis means the point has not moved up or down at all, so its y-coordinate is 0.
misconceptions.2: To the LEFT of the origin means a negative x-coordinate, so x = -3.5.

questions.prompt: Point R has x-coordinate -2. It lies in the second quadrant and is 1.5 units away from the x-axis. What are the coordinates of R? (Quadrants are numbered anticlockwise, starting from the top right: first = top right, second = top left, third = bottom left, fourth = bottom right.)
questions.solution: x = -2 is given. The second quadrant is above the x-axis, so y is positive. 1.5 units from the x-axis means y = 1.5. So R is (-2, 1.5).

misconceptions.1: This point is below the x-axis, in the third quadrant. In the second quadrant, y is positive.
misconceptions.2: The coordinates are the wrong way round. The x-coordinate -2 must come first.
misconceptions.3: This swaps x and y and also puts the point in the third quadrant. Keep x = -2 first, and use y = +1.5 because the second quadrant is above the x-axis.

questions.prompt: A point (a, b) lies in the second quadrant. Which statement must be true? (Quadrants are numbered anticlockwise, starting from the top right: first = top right, second = top left, third = bottom left, fourth = bottom right.)
options: a is positive and b is negative
a and b are both negative
a is negative and b is positive
a and b are both positive
questions.solution: The second quadrant is top left. Left of the y-axis means x (here a) is negative. Above the x-axis means y (here b) is positive.

misconceptions.0: That describes the fourth quadrant (bottom right). The second quadrant is top left.
misconceptions.1: That describes the third quadrant (bottom left).
misconceptions.3: That describes the first quadrant (top right).

questions.prompt: Match each point to where it is on the coordinate grid. (Quadrants are numbered anticlockwise, starting from the top right: first = top right, second = top left, third = bottom left, fourth = bottom right.)
questions.solution: (0, 4): x = 0, so it is on the y-axis. (-4, 0): y = 0, so it is on the x-axis. (-4, -4): both negative, so third quadrant. (4, -4): x positive, y negative, so fourth quadrant.

misconceptions.common: Mixing up the axes: a point with x = 0 is on the y-axis (not the x-axis), and a point with y = 0 is on the x-axis.

questions.prompt: Which of these points is furthest from the x-axis?
questions.solution: Distance from the x-axis = the size of the y-coordinate, ignoring the sign. The distances are 6.5, 3, 6 and 6.25. The largest is 6.5, so (2, -6.5) is furthest.

misconceptions.1: This uses the x-coordinate. The distance from the x-axis is given by the y-coordinate, and that point is only 3 units from the x-axis.
misconceptions.2: The minus sign in -6.5 only tells you the point is BELOW the axis. It is still 6.5 units away, which is more than 6.
misconceptions.3: 6.25 is less than 6.5 (6.25 < 6.50). Comparing '25' with '5' as if they were whole numbers gives the wrong answer.

questions.prompt: Three corners of a rectangle are plotted on the grid. The sides of the rectangle are horizontal and vertical. What are the coordinates of the fourth corner?
questions.solution: The bottom side goes from (1, 1) to (5, 1). The right side goes up to (5, 4), so the top side is at y = 4. The missing corner is straight above (1, 1) and level with (5, 4): (1, 4).

misconceptions.1: The coordinates have been written the wrong way round. The missing corner is above (1, 1), so x stays 1 and y becomes 4.
misconceptions.2: The rectangle is 4 units wide and 3 units tall, not a square. The fourth corner must line up with (1, 1) vertically and with (5, 4) horizontally.
misconceptions.3: This takes the 5 from an x-coordinate and uses it as y. The top side of the rectangle is at y = 4, so the corner is (1, 4).

questions.prompt: The line drawn on the grid goes from (2, 3) to (9, 3). How many units long is the line?
questions.solution: Both ends have y = 3, so the line is horizontal. Its length is the difference between the x-coordinates: 9 - 2 = 7 units. Check by counting the squares along the line on the grid: 7.

misconceptions.common: Adding the x-coordinates (2 + 9 = 11) instead of finding the difference, or counting the grid lines (8) instead of the spaces between them.

questions.skill: lengths of horizontal and vertical lines

questions.prompt: True or false: The line joining (4, -1) and (4, 6) is parallel to the y-axis.
questions.solution: Both points have x-coordinate 4. Every point on the line is 4 units right of the y-axis, so the line is vertical, which means it is parallel to the y-axis. True.

misconceptions.common: Thinking that equal x-coordinates make a horizontal line. Same x means the line goes straight up and down (vertical).

questions.prompt: A line joins (-3, 2) and (5, 2). Which statement describes it?
options: It is parallel to the y-axis
It is parallel to the x-axis
questions.solution: Both points have y = 2, so every point on the line is 2 units above the x-axis. The line is horizontal, which means it is parallel to the x-axis.

misconceptions.0: A line parallel to the y-axis is vertical, and all its points have the same x-coordinate. Here it is the y-coordinates that are the same.
misconceptions.1: A diagonal line changes both x and y. Here y stays at 2 the whole way, so the line is flat.
misconceptions.2: The line crosses the y-axis at (0, 2), not at (0, 0). Crossing an axis is not the same as passing through the origin.

questions.prompt: Three corners of a square are plotted on the grid. What are the coordinates of the fourth corner? Write them like (x, y).
questions.solution: The square has sides of 3 units. From (3, 3) go 3 units left along the top to reach x = 0. The fourth corner is (0, 3), straight above (0, 0).

misconceptions.common: Writing (3, 0), which is already a corner, or swapping the numbers. The missing corner is directly above (0, 0).

questions.prompt: The line drawn on the grid goes from (-3, 2) to (5, 2). How many units long is it?
questions.solution: Both ends have y = 2, so the line is horizontal. From x = -3 to x = 0 is 3 units, and from x = 0 to x = 5 is 5 units. 3 + 5 = 8 units. You can also count the 8 squares along the line, or work out 5 - (-3) = 8.

misconceptions.common: Working out 5 - 3 = 2. When the line crosses the y-axis, add the distance on each side of zero: 3 + 5 = 8.

questions.skill: lengths of horizontal and vertical lines

questions.prompt: The line drawn on the grid goes from (1, -4) to (1, 3). How many units long is it?
questions.solution: Both ends have x = 1, so the line is vertical. From y = -4 up to y = 0 is 4 units, then from 0 up to 3 is 3 units. 4 + 3 = 7 units. Count the squares along the line to check.

misconceptions.common: Working out 4 - 3 = 1. The line crosses the x-axis, so the two parts add: 4 + 3 = 7.

questions.skill: lengths of horizontal and vertical lines

questions.prompt: The line drawn on the grid joins (2, 5) and (8, 5). What are the coordinates of its midpoint?
questions.solution: The line is horizontal at y = 5. It is 8 - 2 = 6 units long, so the midpoint is 3 units along from x = 2: 2 + 3 = 5. Or work out (2 + 8) / 2 = 5. So the midpoint is (5, 5).

misconceptions.0: 6 is the LENGTH of the line (8 - 2). The midpoint is half of that length along from the start: 2 + 3 = 5.
misconceptions.2: This adds the x-coordinates (2 + 8 = 10) but forgets to halve the total.
misconceptions.3: 3 is half the length, but you need to count 3 on from the starting point x = 2, giving x = 5.

questions.skill: midpoints of horizontal and vertical lines

questions.prompt: ABCD is a square. Corners A, B and C are plotted on the grid. What are the coordinates of D?
questions.solution: AB goes 4 units right, so each side is 4 units. B to C goes 4 units up. D is 4 units up from A: (-2, 1 + 4) = (-2, 5). Check on the grid: D is straight above A and level with C, and D to C is 4 units across.

misconceptions.0: The correct numbers but in the wrong order. Write x first: D is at x = -2 (above A) and y = 5 (level with C).
misconceptions.1: This goes 4 units DOWN from A. But B to C goes up, so the square is above side AB and D must be above A.
misconceptions.3: This goes 4 units right from C. The corners go round in order A, B, C, D, so from C you go back LEFT along the top to above A.

questions.prompt: The straight line drawn on the grid passes through (-1, 4) and (6, 4). It carries on in both directions. Select ALL the points that lie on this line.
questions.solution: Both marked points have y = 4, so the line is horizontal: every point on it has y = 4, whatever x is. (2, 4), (-5, 4) and (0, 4) all have y = 4. (-5, 4) is still on the line because the line carries on to the left.

misconceptions.1: (4, 2) has the numbers swapped. Every point on this line has y = 4, so it is (4, 4) that is on the line.
misconceptions.4: (4, 6) is 2 units above the line. Points on the line all have y-coordinate 4.
misconceptions.5: (6, -4) is below the x-axis. The line is at y = +4, not -4.

questions.prompt: ABCD is a parallelogram with its corners in that order, so AB is parallel to DC and BC is parallel to AD. Corners A, B and C are plotted on the grid. What are the coordinates of D?
questions.solution: In a parallelogram, opposite sides are equal and parallel. To get from B (4, 0) to C (6, 3) you go 2 right and 3 up. Do the same from A (0, 0): D = (0 + 2, 0 + 3) = (2, 3). Check: D to C is 4 units right, the same as A to B.

misconceptions.0: This makes a right angle at A, as if the shape were a rectangle. In this parallelogram, side BC slopes 2 right and 3 up, so AD must do the same.
misconceptions.1: This moves 2 LEFT from A. BC goes 2 RIGHT and 3 up, so AD must also go 2 right and 3 up.
misconceptions.2: This adds the x-coordinates of B and C. D is found by doing the same move from A that takes B to C.

questions.prompt: The rectangle is drawn on a grid of 1 cm squares. What is the perimeter of the rectangle in cm?
questions.solution: Width: from x = -3 to x = 5 is 5 - (-3) = 8 cm (count 8 squares along the bottom). Height: from y = -2 to y = 4 is 4 - (-2) = 6 cm (count 6 squares up the side). Perimeter = 8 + 6 + 8 + 6 = 28 cm.

misconceptions.common: Working out 5 - 3 = 2 and 4 - 2 = 2 instead of counting across zero, or finding the area (8 x 6 = 48) instead of the perimeter.

questions.prompt: Two corners of a square, next to each other, are plotted on the grid and joined. Each grid square is 1 cm by 1 cm. What is the area of the square?
questions.solution: The side goes from x = -1 to x = 4, so it is 4 - (-1) = 5 cm long (count 5 squares along it). Area of a square = 5 x 5 = 25 cm^2.

misconceptions.1: This uses 4 - 1 = 3 as the side length. From x = -1 to x = 4 you cross zero: 1 + 4 = 5 cm.
misconceptions.2: This is 4 x 5, which is the perimeter of the square (4 sides of 5 cm), not the area.
misconceptions.3: This is 5 x 2, doubling the side instead of squaring it. Area of a square = side x side.

questions.prompt: The line drawn on the grid joins (-3, 1) and (-3, 8). What are the coordinates of its midpoint?
questions.solution: The line is vertical (both ends have x = -3), so the midpoint has x = -3. Halfway between y = 1 and y = 8: (1 + 8) / 2 = 9 / 2 = 4.5. Midpoint = (-3, 4.5).

misconceptions.0: 3.5 is half the LENGTH of the line (7 / 2). You must count 3.5 up from the start, y = 1, giving 4.5.
misconceptions.2: The line is vertical, so every point on it has x = -3. Do not halve the x-coordinate.
misconceptions.3: This adds the y-coordinates (1 + 8 = 9) but forgets to divide by 2.

questions.skill: midpoints of horizontal and vertical lines

questions.prompt: The rectangle is drawn on the grid. What are the coordinates of the centre of the rectangle? Write them like (x, y).
questions.solution: The centre is halfway across and halfway up. Halfway between x = -4 and x = 2: (-4 + 2) / 2 = -1. Halfway between y = -1 and y = 3: (-1 + 3) / 2 = 1. Centre = (-1, 1). On the grid: the rectangle is 6 squares wide, so go 3 squares right from x = -4; it is 4 squares tall, so go 2 squares up from y = -1.

misconceptions.common: Halving the width (6 / 2 = 3) and using 3 as the x-coordinate. You must count 3 on from x = -4, which gives -1.

questions.skill: midpoints of horizontal and vertical lines

questions.prompt: True or false: The shape drawn on the grid is a square.
questions.solution: Bottom side: from x = 2 to x = 5 is 3 units. Right side: from y = 1 to y = 5 is 4 units. The sides are not all the same length, so the shape is a rectangle but NOT a square. False.

misconceptions.common: Seeing four right angles (the sides are horizontal and vertical) and assuming it is a square. A square also needs all four sides equal, so check the lengths: 3 units across but 4 units up.

questions.prompt: Point A is plotted on the grid. It is translated 4 units to the right. What are the coordinates of its image?
questions.solution: A is (2, 3). Moving right adds to the x-coordinate: 2 + 4 = 6. The y-coordinate does not change. Image = (6, 3).

misconceptions.0: This moves the point 4 units UP. Moving right changes the x-coordinate, not the y-coordinate.
misconceptions.1: This moves the point 4 units to the LEFT (2 - 4 = -2). Right means add to x.
misconceptions.3: Only x should change. Moving right adds 4 to x; the y-coordinate stays at 3.

questions.prompt: Point B is plotted on the grid. It is translated 3 units down. What are the coordinates of its image?
questions.solution: B is (5, 1). Down changes y: 1 - 3 = -2 (count 3 squares down on the grid, past the x-axis). x stays at 5. Image = (5, -2).

misconceptions.0: This moves the point UP (1 + 3 = 4). Moving down subtracts from y: 1 - 3 = -2.
misconceptions.1: This moves the point 3 units left. Down changes the y-coordinate, not the x-coordinate.
misconceptions.2: 1 - 3 is -2, not 2. Going down past 0 takes you into negative numbers.

questions.prompt: Point C is plotted on the grid. It is translated 2 units left and 3 units down. Where is its image?

misconceptions.1: This moves 2 units RIGHT (-1 + 2 = 1). Left means subtract from x: -1 - 2 = -3.
misconceptions.2: This moves 3 units UP. Down means subtract from y: 4 - 3 = 1.
misconceptions.3: The two amounts have been swapped (3 left and 2 down). Read carefully: 2 left, 3 down.

questions.prompt: True or false: When a shape is translated, it becomes bigger or smaller.
questions.solution: A translation only slides a shape to a new position. It does not turn, flip or resize it. The image is exactly the same size and shape. So the statement is false.

misconceptions.common: Confusing a translation (a slide) with an enlargement. Every point moves the same distance in the same direction, so the size cannot change.

questions.prompt: Point P moves to P' by a translation, as shown by the arrow on the grid. Describe the translation.
questions.solution: P is (1, -2) and P' is (6, 1). Change in x: 6 - 1 = 5, so 5 units right. Change in y: from -2 up to 1 is 3 units (2 up to 0, then 1 more), so 3 units up. Count the squares on the grid to check.

misconceptions.0: This is the move from the IMAGE back to the original. Going from (1, -2) to (6, 1), x gets bigger (right) and y gets bigger (up).
misconceptions.2: The two amounts are swapped. The change in x (1 to 6) is 5, and the change in y (-2 to 1) is 3.
misconceptions.3: From y = -2 to y = 1 you pass 0: 2 units up to 0, then 1 more, which is 3 units, not 1.

questions.prompt: Point Q is translated 4 units right and 2 units up. Its image Q' is plotted on the grid. Where was Q before the translation?
questions.solution: Work backwards from Q'(0, -3): undo 4 right by going 4 left, and undo 2 up by going 2 down. x = 0 - 4 = -4, y = -3 - 2 = -5. Q was at (-4, -5). Check: (-4, -5) moved 4 right and 2 up is (0, -3).

misconceptions.0: This applies the translation to the image again. To go backwards, undo it: move 4 LEFT and 2 DOWN.
misconceptions.1: The x part has been undone correctly, but the y part has not. Undo 2 up by going 2 down: -3 - 2 = -5.
misconceptions.2: The y part is right, but undoing 4 right means going 4 LEFT: 0 - 4 = -4.

questions.skill: finding the original point before a translation

questions.prompt: Triangle ABC is drawn on the grid. It is translated 3 units left and 2 units up. What are the coordinates of the image of C?
questions.solution: C is (1, 5). Left 3: 1 - 3 = -2. Up 2: 5 + 2 = 7. The image of C is (-2, 7).

misconceptions.1: This moves 3 units RIGHT. Left means subtract from x: 1 - 3 = -2.
misconceptions.2: This moves 2 units DOWN. Up means add to y: 5 + 2 = 7.
misconceptions.3: The amounts are swapped (2 left, 3 up). It should be 3 left and 2 up.

questions.prompt: A shape is translated on a grid. Select ALL the statements that are always true.
options: The image is the same size as the original
The image is the same shape as the original
The image is a mirror image (flipped over) of the original
Every point of the shape moves the same distance in the same direction
questions.solution: A translation is a slide. Every point moves the same distance in the same direction, so the image has the same size, the same shape and faces the same way. It is not flipped or turned.

misconceptions.2: Flipping over is a reflection. A translation only slides, so the image faces the same way as the original.
misconceptions.4: Turning is a rotation. In a translation the shape does not turn at all.

questions.prompt: The square is drawn on the grid. It is translated 6 units to the left. What is the x-coordinate of the image of corner P?
questions.solution: P is (5, 5). Left 6 means subtract 6 from x: 5 - 6 = -1. The y-coordinate stays 5, so the image of P is (-1, 5) and its x-coordinate is -1.

misconceptions.common: Answering 1 instead of -1. 5 - 6 goes one step past zero, into the negative numbers.

questions.prompt: Triangle ABC is drawn on the grid. It is translated 2 units right and 5 units down. Match each corner to its image.

diagram.alt: A coordinate grid with four quadrants, x from -5 to 5 and y from -4 to 7. Triangle ABC is drawn with corners A(-3, 4), B(0, 2) and C(1.5, 6).

questions.solution: Add 2 to every x-coordinate and subtract 5 from every y-coordinate. A: (-3 + 2, 4 - 5) = (-1, -1). B: (0 + 2, 2 - 5) = (2, -3). C: (1.5 + 2, 6 - 5) = (3.5, 1).

misconceptions.common: Moving in the opposite directions (left and up), which sends A to (-5, 9), or swapping the amounts (5 right and 2 down), which sends B to (5, 0).

questions.prompt: Point P is translated 3 units right and 4 units down. Its image is P'(1, -1). Then P' is translated 2 units left and 6 units up to give P''. Which single translation would move P straight to P''?
questions.solution: Work out P first: undo the first move from P'(1, -1). P = (1 - 3, -1 + 4) = (-2, 3). Then P'' = (1 - 2, -1 + 6) = (-1, 5). From P(-2, 3) to P''(-1, 5): x goes up by 1 (right 1) and y goes up by 2 (up 2). Shortcut: 3 right then 2 left = 1 right; 4 down then 6 up = 2 up.

misconceptions.0: This is the move from P'' back to P, the opposite direction.
misconceptions.1: This adds all the numbers without noticing that right and left (and down and up) cancel each other out.
misconceptions.3: Across, 3 right and then 2 LEFT leaves only 1 unit right overall, not 5.

questions.prompt: Rectangle ABCD is drawn on the grid. It is translated so that corner A moves to A', as shown by the arrow. What are the coordinates of the image of corner C? Write them like (x, y).
questions.solution: First find the translation from the arrow: A(-2, 1) to A'(1, -3) is 3 units right (1 - (-2) = 3) and 4 units down (-3 - 1 = -4). Every corner moves the same way. C(3, 4) moves to (3 + 3, 4 - 4) = (6, 0).

misconceptions.common: Moving C straight to A'(1, -3), or using the wrong direction for the translation. Find the movement from A to A' first (3 right, 4 down), then apply it to C.

questions.prompt: True or false: A translation of 4 units left and 1 unit up moves the point (3, 0) to (-1, 1).
questions.solution: Left 4: 3 - 4 = -1. Up 1: 0 + 1 = 1. The image is (-1, 1), so the statement is true.

misconceptions.common: Working out 3 - 4 as 1. Counting back 4 from 3 goes past zero to -1.

questions.prompt: Point P (2.5, -1) moves to P' (-1, 1.5) by a translation, as shown by the arrow on the grid. How many units to the LEFT did it move?

diagram.alt: A coordinate grid with four quadrants, x from -3 to 5 and y from -3 to 3. Point P is plotted at (2.5, -1) and point P' at (-1, 1.5). An arrow goes from P to P'.

questions.solution: Look at the x-coordinates: 2.5 to -1. From 2.5 down to 0 is 2.5 units, and from 0 to -1 is 1 more unit. 2.5 + 1 = 3.5 units left. (It also moved 2.5 units up, from -1 to 1.5.)

misconceptions.common: Working out 2.5 - 1 = 1.5. Because the point crosses the y-axis, you must add the distances on each side of zero: 2.5 + 1 = 3.5.

questions.prompt: Points A, B, C and D are plotted on the grid, one in each quadrant. Match each point to its coordinates.

diagram.alt: A coordinate grid with four quadrants, x from -5 to 5 and y from -5 to 5. Points A, B, C and D are plotted, one in each quadrant.

questions.solution: Read across first (x), then up or down (y). A: 3 right, 2 up = (3, 2). B: 4 left, 1 up = (-4, 1). C: 2 left, 3 down = (-2, -3). D: 1 right, 4 down = (1, -4).

misconceptions.common: (2, 3) and (-3, -2) have the numbers the wrong way round. Always go along the x-axis first (left or right), then up or down. Left of the y-axis or below the x-axis gives a negative number.

questions.prompt: Point K is plotted on the grid. What are the coordinates of K? Write them like (x, y).

diagram.alt: A coordinate grid with four quadrants, x from -5 to 5 and y from -5 to 5, with point K plotted in the top-left quadrant.

questions.solution: Start at the origin. K is 3 squares to the LEFT, so x = -3. It is 4 squares UP, so y = 4. Write x first: (-3, 4).

misconceptions.common: Writing (4, -3) or (3, 4). Go across first, then up. Left of the y-axis means the x-coordinate is negative.

questions.prompt: Point M is plotted on the grid. What are the coordinates of M? Write them like (x, y).

diagram.alt: A coordinate grid with four quadrants, x from -5 to 5 and y from -5 to 5, with point M plotted in the bottom-left quadrant, halfway between two vertical grid lines.

questions.solution: M is to the left of the y-axis, exactly halfway between x = -2 and x = -3, so x = -2.5 (or -2 1/2). M is 3 squares below the x-axis, so y = -3. M is (-2.5, -3).

misconceptions.common: Rounding to the nearest grid line and writing -2 or -3 for x. M sits halfway between -2 and -3, which is -2.5. Also check both signs: M is to the left and below, so both numbers are negative.

questions.prompt: Four points are plotted on the grid. Which point is at (-2, 3)?

diagram.alt: A coordinate grid with four quadrants, x from -5 to 5 and y from -5 to 5, with points A, B, C and D plotted.

questions.solution: (-2, 3) means start at the origin, go 2 units LEFT (x = -2), then 3 units UP (y = 3). Point B is there.

misconceptions.0: Point A is at (3, -2). That uses the numbers the wrong way round. For (-2, 3), go across first: 2 to the LEFT, then 3 UP.
misconceptions.2: Point C is at (2, 3), to the right of the y-axis. The minus sign in -2 means go LEFT, not right.
misconceptions.3: Point D is at (-3, 2): 3 left and 2 up. For (-2, 3) you go 2 left and 3 up. The first number is always the move across.

questions.prompt: Four points are plotted on the axes of the grid. Which point is at (0, -3)?

diagram.alt: A coordinate grid with four quadrants, x from -5 to 5 and y from -5 to 5, with points A, B, C and D plotted on the axes.

questions.solution: In (0, -3), x = 0 means no move left or right, so the point is on the y-axis. y = -3 means 3 units DOWN from the origin. Point C is there.

misconceptions.0: Point A is at (-3, 0), on the x-axis. In (0, -3) the x-coordinate is 0, so the point has not moved left or right: it is on the y-axis.
misconceptions.1: Point B is at (0, 3), above the origin. -3 is negative, so the point is 3 units DOWN.
misconceptions.3: Point D is at (3, 0), on the x-axis. x = 0 means the point is on the y-axis, and y = -3 means 3 units below the origin.

questions.prompt: ABCD is a rectangle. Corners A, B and C are plotted on the grid and joined. What are the coordinates of D?
questions.solution: Read the corners: A(-3, -2), B(4, -2), C(4, 1). D must be straight above A (same x as A, so x = -3) and level with C (same y as C, so y = 1). D is (-3, 1).

misconceptions.0: (1, -3) has the numbers the wrong way round. D is above A, so x = -3, and level with C, so y = 1. Write x first: (-3, 1).
misconceptions.1: D is level with C, which is ABOVE the x-axis at y = 1. So the y-coordinate of D is 1, not -1.
misconceptions.2: D is straight above A, which is to the LEFT of the y-axis at x = -3. So the x-coordinate of D is -3, not 3.

questions.prompt: ABCD is a square standing on one corner. Corners A, B and C are plotted on the grid and joined. What are the coordinates of D? Write them like (x, y).
questions.solution: Read the corners: A(-1, 1), B(2, -2), C(5, 1). From B to C you go 3 right and 3 up. In a square, opposite sides are equal and parallel, so from A to D is the same move: 3 right and 3 up. D = (-1 + 3, 1 + 3) = (2, 4). Check: D to C is 3 right and 3 down, the same as A to B.

misconceptions.common: Putting D level with A or C as if the sides were flat, which gives (-1, 4) or (5, 4). This square is tilted, so copy the move from B to C (3 right, 3 up), starting at A.

questions.prompt: ABCD is a parallelogram with its corners in that order. Corners A, B and C are plotted on the grid and joined. What are the coordinates of D?
questions.solution: Read the corners: A(-4, -2), B(1, -2), C(3, 2). From B to C you go 2 right and 4 up. AD is parallel to BC and the same length, so from A make the same move: D = (-4 + 2, -2 + 4) = (-2, 2). Check: D to C is 5 units right, the same as A to B.

misconceptions.0: (-4, 2) puts D straight above A, which would make a rectangle. In this parallelogram BC slopes 2 right and 4 up, so AD must slope the same way.
misconceptions.1: This moves 2 LEFT from A. B to C goes 2 RIGHT and 4 up, so from A you must also go 2 right and 4 up.
misconceptions.3: The signs are the wrong way round. D is to the left of the y-axis (x = -2) and above the x-axis (y = 2).

questions.prompt: Line EF is drawn on the grid. How many units long is EF?
questions.solution: EF is a vertical line, so count the squares from E up to F. From E (y = -5) up to the x-axis is 5 units, and from the x-axis up to F (y = 4) is 4 units. 5 + 4 = 9 units.

misconceptions.common: Working out 5 - 4 = 1, or counting the grid lines (10) instead of the spaces between them. When a line crosses an axis, add the parts on each side: 5 + 4 = 9.

questions.skill: lengths of horizontal and vertical lines

questions.prompt: Shape T is translated to the dashed shape T' on the grid. Describe the translation.
questions.solution: Pick one corner and follow it. The right-angle corner of T at (-4, 1) moves to (1, -2) on T'. Change in x: -4 to 1 is 5 units right. Change in y: 1 to -2 is 3 units down. So the translation is 5 units right and 3 units down.

misconceptions.0: The two amounts are swapped. Follow one corner: it moves 5 squares to the right, then 3 squares down.
misconceptions.2: This is the move from T' back to T. The question asks how T moves to T', so go from the solid shape to the dashed shape.
misconceptions.3: T' is lower on the grid than T, so the shape moved DOWN, not up.

questions.prompt: Triangle PQR is drawn on the grid. It is translated by the move shown by the arrow. What are the coordinates of the image of Q? Write them like (x, y).
questions.solution: First read the arrow: it starts at (1, -4) and ends at (5, -2), so the move is 4 units right and 2 units up. Q is at (-2, 0). Move it the same way: (-2 + 4, 0 + 2) = (2, 2).

misconceptions.common: Giving the end of the arrow, (5, -2), as the answer. The arrow only shows the size and direction of the move (4 right, 2 up). Apply that move to Q.

questions.prompt: The rectangle is drawn on a grid of 1 cm squares. What is the area of the rectangle in cm^2?
questions.solution: Count the squares along the bottom: from x = -4 to x = 2 is 6 cm. Count up the side: from y = -3 to y = 2 is 5 cm. Area = 6 x 5 = 30 cm^2. (You can also count the squares inside: 5 rows of 6.)

misconceptions.common: Finding the perimeter (6 + 5 + 6 + 5 = 22 cm) instead of the area, or working out 4 - 2 = 2 for the width. The width crosses the y-axis: 4 squares on the left and 2 on the right make 6.

questions.prompt: Which grid shows the point P at (-3, 2)?

optionDiagrams.alt: Grid A: a coordinate grid with one point plotted.
Grid B: a coordinate grid with one point plotted.
Grid C: a coordinate grid with one point plotted.
Grid D: a coordinate grid with one point plotted.

questions.solution: (-3, 2): start at the origin, go 3 units LEFT (x = -3), then 2 units UP (y = 2). That is in the top-left part of the grid. Only Grid C has P there.

misconceptions.0: Grid A shows (2, -3): the numbers are the wrong way round. Go across first: 3 to the LEFT, then 2 UP.
misconceptions.1: Grid B shows (3, 2), to the right of the y-axis. The minus sign in -3 means go LEFT.
misconceptions.3: Grid D shows (-3, -2), below the x-axis. The 2 in (-3, 2) is positive, so the point is 2 units UP.

questions.prompt: Triangle T is translated 3 units right and 2 units down. Which diagram shows T and its image (dashed) correctly?
questions.solution: Follow one corner. The right-angle corner of T at (-3, 1) moves 3 right to x = 0 and 2 down to y = -1, so it goes to (0, -1). Only Diagram D has the dashed triangle's right-angle corner at (0, -1), with the same shape facing the same way.

misconceptions.0: In Diagram A the image has moved 2 units UP. Moving down makes the y-coordinates smaller, so the image should be lower than T.
misconceptions.1: In Diagram B the amounts are swapped: the image moved 2 right and 3 down. Check one corner: it must move 3 squares across and 2 squares down.
misconceptions.2: In Diagram C the image has moved 3 units LEFT. Moving right makes the x-coordinates bigger, so the image should be to the right of T.

questions.prompt: Which grid shows the point Q at (0, -2.5)?

optionDiagrams.alt: Grid A: a coordinate grid with one point plotted.
Grid B: a coordinate grid with one point plotted.
Grid C: a coordinate grid with one point plotted.
Grid D: a coordinate grid with one point plotted.

questions.solution: x = 0 means the point is on the y-axis. y = -2.5 means 2 1/2 units DOWN from the origin, halfway between -2 and -3. Only Grid D shows this.

misconceptions.0: Grid A shows (-2.5, 0), on the x-axis. In (0, -2.5) the x-coordinate is 0, so the point is on the y-axis.
misconceptions.1: Grid B shows (0, 2.5), above the origin. -2.5 is negative, so the point is 2.5 units BELOW the origin.
misconceptions.2: Grid C shows (0, -2), exactly on a grid line. -2.5 is halfway between -2 and -3, so the point sits between two grid lines.

questions.prompt: True or false: Point B on the grid is at (4, -2).

diagram.alt: A coordinate grid with four quadrants, x from -5 to 5 and y from -5 to 5, with point B plotted in the top-left quadrant.

questions.solution: Read across first: B is 2 units to the LEFT of the origin, so x = -2. Then up: B is 4 units UP, so y = 4. B is at (-2, 4), not (4, -2). False.

misconceptions.common: (4, -2) uses the numbers the wrong way round. Always read across (x) first, then up or down (y).

questions.prompt: Six points are plotted on the grid. Select ALL the points that are exactly 3 units from the y-axis.
questions.solution: The y-axis is the up-and-down line through 0. Count how many squares across each point is from it: A 3, B 3 (to the left), C 1, D 3, E 1, F 0. So A, B and D.

misconceptions.2: C is at (1, 3). It is 3 units from the x-axis (3 up), but only 1 unit from the y-axis.
misconceptions.4: E is at (-1, -3). It is 3 units below the x-axis, but only 1 unit from the y-axis.
misconceptions.5: F is at (0, 3), ON the y-axis, so it is 0 units from it. Its 3 is the distance from the x-axis.
misconceptions.common: Distance from the y-axis is how far left or right the point is: the x-coordinate without its sign. B at x = -3 counts too: it is 3 units to the left.
